text:
maria (sec-eng): quick heads-up — found a RoleBinding in cluster-prod that is effectively granting `system:nodes` access to the gpu-pool namespace via a ClusterRoleRef. looks like node identities can `impersonate` SA tokens.

alex (infra): whoa, can you paste the binding?

maria (sec-eng): `kubectl -n gpu-pool get rolebinding legacy-gpu-admin -o yaml` shows `roleRef: name: cluster-admin` and `subjects: - kind: Group name: system:nodes`.

chen (sre): that explains the odd `create` events in audit logs we saw yesterday — nodes creating secrets in gpu-pool.

sam (platform): is this from the old migration job? we had a script that converted some namesp-scoped bindings -> clusterroleref for convenience back in 2023.

maria (sec-eng): likely. also noticed audit forwarding to Splunk dropped those encrypted payloads around the same window. KMS unwrap failing when forwarder tries to re-encrypt. error in forwarder: `kms: Decrypt failed: key version mismatch`.

security-bot: created incident INC-5987 (severity: high) — @maria assigned.

alex (infra): immediate mitigation: remove the Group subject and replace with explicit ServiceAccount subjects limited to the controller SAs. can we patch with a namespaced Role/RoleBinding instead of ClusterRoleRef?

maria (sec-eng): yep. proposed quick fix: `kubectl -n gpu-pool apply -f -` with payload: 
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: gpu-pool-node-limited
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "secrets"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: gpu-pool-node-limited-binding
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: gpu-node-proxy
  namespace: kube-system
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: gpu-pool-node-limited
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

alex (infra): do `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:node get secrets -n gpu-pool` before/after to validate.

chen (sre): we should also rotate tokens for the impacted SAs and revoke any long-lived kubeconfig that references `system:nodes` creds.

maria (sec-eng): auditforwarder: check — looks like the forwarder attempted to rewrap logs with customer KMS key (aws:kms arn) and failed because of a previously rotated key_version. Splunk got a 403 and dropped payloads. auditbot: can you list matching log IDs?

auditbot: found 23 dropped events between 3344920000 and 3345003000 with error "KMS_DECRYPT_VERSION_MISMATCH". IDs: [logs/3344920012, logs/3344952103, logs/3344999999]

sam (platform): critical: those dropped events include the `create secret` entries. we need to ingest raw copies from the cluster audit store before we rotated keys. run `gcloud storage cp gs://redwood-audit-archive/33449* /tmp` or S3 equivalent.

maria (sec-eng): I've applied the namespaced Role/RoleBinding and removed the ClusterRoleRef binding (rolled back legacy-gpu-admin). will monitor. patched in prod-1 and prod-2.

alex (infra): thanks. next steps:
- add admission webhook check to block RoleBindings that bind `system:nodes` to cluster roles
- add CI test `ci/verify_rbac` that asserts no ClusterRoleRef to node groups exist
- add an alert `RBAC-Anomaly: ClusterRoleBinding to system:nodes`

chen (sre): also add an e2e that runs `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:node` across namespaces and fails CI if any privileged verbs returned.

maria (sec-eng): security postmortem + timeline. start draft (I'll share). include KMS forwarder config change: auto-fallback to sending raw (unencrypted) to retention bucket when rewrap fails, and an alert for KMS rewrap failures.

security-bot: noted action items and owners: patch-rolebinding (alex), rotate-sa (chen), pull-archive-logs (sam), pm (maria).

sam (platform): small follow-up — we should avoid deleting the existing binding until we confirm no active workloads rely on node impersonation. will cordon a small nodepool and test.

maria (sec-eng): agreed. did a canary on a culled nodepool; no downstream failures observed. rolling removal now.

alex (infra): when this is closed, add the verification to the cluster creation template so new clusters don't recreate the legacy binding.

chen (sre): thanks all. adding runbook notes under /runbooks/rbac-least-privilege.md and creating an automated watch job.

maria (sec-eng): thanks team :thumbsup: I'll open the postmortem and link logs + hardened policy snippets.

security-bot: incident INC-5987 status -> mitigated, monitoring.
